story.title: IQ Riddles
story.midCtaText: Enjoying the quiz? Subscribe & hit the bell!
story.subscribeText: New quiz every day – turn on the bell 🔔

questions.q: 3 haystacks here, 5 there. Put them all **together**. How many?
A rooster lays an egg on a **roof**. Which way does it roll?
Doctor: **3 pills**, one every 30 minutes. How long do they last?
Divide **30 by half**, then add 10. What do you get?
How many times does the digit **9** appear from 1 to 100?
Snail: up 3 m by day, down 2 m by night. **10 m wall**. Days?
Dad is **4×** his son's age. In 20 years, 2×. Son's age now?

lines.q: Twelve hard riddles, and most people solve three. Can you solve five? Round one, easy. What comes next? One, four, nine, sixteen, twenty five...
lines.a: Thirty six! They're square numbers. Six times six.

lines.q: A farmer has three haystacks in one field and five in another. He puts them all together. How many haystacks does he have?
lines.a: One! One giant haystack. Words beat maths on that one.

lines.q: A rooster lays an egg right on top of a barn roof. Which way does the egg roll?
lines.a: There's no egg! Roosters don't lay eggs. Only hens do.

lines.q: Round two, medium. A doctor gives you three pills and says, take one every half hour. How long until they're all gone?
lines.a: One hour! First pill now, second at thirty minutes, third at sixty.

lines.q: Divide thirty by a half, then add ten. What do you get?
lines.a: Seventy! Dividing by a half doubles it. Sixty plus ten.

lines.q: What comes next? One, one, two, three, five, eight...
lines.a: Thirteen! Add the last two numbers. If you're enjoying this, subscribe and turn on the bell!

lines.q: Which number is the odd one out? Eight, twenty seven, sixty four, one hundred, one hundred and twenty five.
lines.a: One hundred! All the others are cube numbers. How are you doing so far?

lines.q: Round three, hard. Count from one to one hundred. How many times do you write the digit nine?
lines.a: Twenty! Ten in the ones place, and ten more in the nineties. Ninety nine counts twice.

lines.q: A snail climbs three metres up a ten metre wall every day, and slides back two metres every night. How many days to reach the top?
lines.a: Eight days! After seven nights it's at seven metres, then it climbs out on day eight.

lines.q: Which word doesn't belong with listen? Silent, stolen, tinsel, or enlist?
lines.a: Stolen! The others use the exact same letters as listen. Three left, stay with me!

lines.q: Final round, legend. What comes next? Two, three, five, nine, seventeen...
lines.a: Thirty three! Double it and take away one, every time.

lines.q: Final question. A dad is four times as old as his son. In twenty years, he'll be only twice as old. How old is the son now?
lines.a: Ten! Dad is forty. In twenty years, sixty and thirty. Exactly double.
